name: Tubal (Son of Japheth)
title: Ancestor of peoples in Asia Minor
summary: Tubal was one of Japheth's seven sons and a grandson of Noah. He is regarded as the ancestor of the peoples in eastern Asia Minor (modern-day Turkey/Caucasus region). Tubal is mentioned several times in the Old Testament, both in the table of nations in Genesis and in prophetic texts by Isaiah and Ezekiel, where his descendants are linked to trade and military power.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the table of nations after the Flood
keyEvents.description: Tubal is listed as one of Japheth's seven sons in the table of nations in Genesis 10, which describes how the peoples of the earth spread out after the Flood.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in the genealogy of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Tubal is mentioned again as a son of Japheth in the great genealogy in 1 Chronicles, confirming his place among the patriarchs of the nations.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy about distant nations
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah mentions Tubal among the distant nations who will see God's glory and proclaim His praise among the Gentiles.

keyEvents.title: Tubal's trade described by Ezekiel
keyEvents.description: In Ezekiel's lament over Tyre, Tubal and Meshech are mentioned as trading partners who dealt in slaves and bronze goods with the great commercial city.

keyEvents.title: Tubal in the prophecy against Gog
keyEvents.description: Ezekiel prophesies against Gog, prince of Meshech and Tubal, predicting a great end-time battle where God will judge these nations.

keyEvents.title: The fall of Tubal into Sheol
keyEvents.description: In Ezekiel's prophecy about the fall of the nations, Tubal and Meshech are mentioned among the mighty nations that have gone down to Sheol because of their violence and wickedness.
